problem: The VLN field has produced many tasks, datasets and method families (indoor, outdoor, interactive, multimodal-instruction) that are hard to compare, and no single scaffold organizes them along shared assumptions.
motivation: VLN is a core testbed for embodied AI and for home robots, driving assistance and accessibility. Rapid growth of benchmarks and methods calls for a structured view of task assumptions, evaluation metrics and technique evolution, so that open challenges can be identified.
key_idea: Organize VLN tasks with a four-way taxonomy (Indoor, Outdoor, Interactive, Multimodal-instruction) and review methods as modular, end-to-end IL/RL, pre-training, and memory/graph-structured families.
insight: The survey argues VLN methods have moved from engineered modularity to learned end-to-end models and now to hybrids that keep structure (topological maps, memory) for long-horizon reasoning and generalization. Pre-training is presented as foundational for data efficiency. It identifies sim-to-real gap, long-horizon planning, interactive reasoning and metric limitations as main open problems. There are no experiments or ablations; these are qualitative conclusions.
method: Four-quadrant taxonomy: categorizes VLN tasks by environment (indoor/outdoor), interaction (non-interactive/interactive) and instruction modality (language-only/multimodal).
Dataset review: covers R2R, REVERIE, CVDN, Touchdown, Talk2Nav, ALFRED, TEACh, GesNavi and sketch-based navigation, with metrics and challenges (Table 1).

Method families: modular (TPT), end-to-end IL (Speaker-Follower) and RL (RCM+SIL, EnvDrop), hybrid (DAgger, model-based RL), pre-training (VLN-BERT, ProbES, YouTube-VLN, BEVBert), memory/graph (E.T., MemoNav, DUET, ETPNav, PRET), compared in Table 2.
Challenge analysis: discusses sim-to-real gap, long-horizon planning, interactive reasoning, generalization and evaluation limits, and deployment constraints such as compute, safety and bias.
Future directions: higher-fidelity simulation and data, world models, LLM/VLM plus robotics integration, embodied multimodal learning, and fairer benchmarks.
numbers_note: Survey paper with no experimental results.
results: This is a qualitative review with no new experiments or quantitative comparisons. Its main contributions are the four-quadrant task taxonomy and the comparative tables of datasets and method families.
limitations: No quantitative benchmark comparison or results tables; coverage is qualitative and largely predates LLM/VLM-based navigation agents.
Citations and references are inconsistent (numbering mismatches, duplicate GesNavi entries), and the indoor section ends on an unfinished sentence.
Many methods (TPT, IPPD, PRET, MemoNav) are described briefly without citations.
